subject: Review request: policy engine precedence changes for Route-level A/B experiments (Phase 0)
related_links: Linear: PM-481 (route-level A/B testing PRD + GA criteria)
body:
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 9:14 AM PST
Subject: Review request: policy engine precedence changes for Route-level A/B experiments (Phase 0)

Dylan / Marissa / Sean,

We’re at the point in Phase 0 where we need explicit sign-off on the policy engine precedence changes to support route-level A/B experiments in Console.

This is the “routing truth table” portion that will impact canaries, model pinning, and fallback behavior, so I’d like to lock it before we let ENG-2841 proceed beyond implementation details.

Requested review/approval (by EOD Mon 2/16 ideally):

1) Precedence between:
   - route-level A/B experiment assignment
   - existing canary rollout policies
   - fallback routing (capacity + reliability)
   - model pinning (customer-specified)

2) Definition of “measurement vs reliability” boundaries:
   - When guardrails trip (latency / error), do we automatically override the experiment assignment?
   - If yes, do we emit an exposure with a “forced_fallback” reason, or treat as non-exposure?

3) Operational behavior:
   - What is the expected behavior when the assignment service is unavailable? (fail open to control vs fail closed)
   - How do we keep assignment stable across retries / stream reconnect without causing cardinality/PII issues?

Docs/links:
- ADR draft 0187 (deterministic assignment + bucketing + stickiness): Confluence link in related_links
- ADR draft 0188 (exposure logging + privacy + retention): Confluence link in related_links
- Linear epic: ENG-2841
- Draft PR (policy engine model changes + precedence plumbing): redwood/pr_18357_policy-engine-support-experiment-config

Context: This is specifically for route-level experiments (e.g., /v1/chat/completions per project/tenant) where Console config defines the split and eligibility rules. We’re aiming for something that is safe for Hosted + Dedicated beta. Private may be gated.

If you’d prefer, I can do a 20-min review live, but written approval on the ADRs is the easiest audit trail for later.

Thanks,
Priya
Platform org sponsor
Redwood Inference

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 11:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Review request: policy engine precedence changes for Route-level A/B experiments (Phase 0)

Thanks Priya — took a pass through ADR-0187 + the PR.

Two questions before I can give a 👍:

1) Precedence: In the draft, it reads like experiment assignment happens “after” canary evaluation, which would mean a canary could change which variant someone sees. That feels surprising for measurement.

Is the intended order:
   eligibility -> experiment assignment -> variant-specific policy -> fallback?

2) Failure mode: For assignment service unavailability, the PR seems to default to “control” (variant A) silently. That’s probably right, but I want to make sure Console results UI will reflect the drop in exposures rather than implying variant A ‘won’ due to skew.

Also: can we guarantee we won’t generate a new variant assignment on retry if request_id changes? (streaming reconnect is the big one we’ve seen in other features)

If you can clarify those in the ADR text, I’m happy to sign off.

-Dylan
Engineering Lead, Console & Tooling


---

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 12, 2026 at 1:37 PM PST
Subject: Re: Review request: policy engine precedence changes for Route-level A/B experiments (Phase 0)

Good catches — aligned with your instincts.

1) Precedence (updated intent)
We want *measurement stickiness* to be the primary behavior, with reliability as an override.

Proposed order (I’ll update ADR-0187 + the PR comments to reflect this explicitly):

A) Determine whether the request is eligible for an experiment (route + tenant/project + region + time window).
B) If eligible, compute deterministic assignment (variant A/B) using stable hash inputs.
C) Apply variant-specific config (model version, quantization profile, etc.)
D) Apply existing safety constraints (capacity / routing constraints) and *then* fallback policies as needed.

So: canaries do NOT “wrap” experiments. If a route has an active experiment, we treat it as the rollout mechanism for that route; canary policies would be rejected as overlapping at validation time (Console will warn / block).

2) Failure mode + exposure semantics
- If assignment service unavailable: route continues with control variant (A) but we emit a *separate* health counter and we do NOT emit an experiment exposure event (so reporting won’t misinterpret it as A exposure).
- If fallback override happens after assignment (e.g., variant B capacity constrained): emit exposure with outcome_reason="forced_fallback" and include the originally assigned variant + the actually served variant. (No request-level identifiers beyond what’s already approved in ADR-0188.)

3) Retry / streaming reconnect stability
We’re avoiding request_id for this reason.
Hash inputs in ADR-0187 draft are:
- tenant_id (required)
- project_id (required)
- route_id (required)
- plus “stickiness key”: api_key_id when present; otherwise a stable header (x-redwood-user-id) when configured; otherwise falls back to tenant/project only.

We also add a “stickiness window” option (default 24h) so assignment stays consistent even if some upstream IDs aren’t present on every request.

Sean: I called out the “no exposure on assignment outage” in the guardrails section; please confirm it aligns with SRE expectations for alerting.

I’ll push the ADR edits this afternoon and tag you both in Confluence for approval.

Priya

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, Feb 13, 2026 at 8:02 AM PST
Subject: Re: Review request: policy engine precedence changes for Route-level A/B experiments (Phase 0)

This works for Product.

+1 to:
- experiments acting as the rollout mechanism for the route (block overlapping canaries in Console validation)
- forced_fallback being explicit in exposure events so results UI can show “served != assigned” and we can message it clearly
- no-exposure when assignment is down (but surface “assignment degraded” prominently in the UI)

Once the ADR text is updated, I’ll approve in Confluence.

Marissa
Product Lead, Console & Rollouts
Redwood Inference
